name: @olai/tests
//exports: THE HARNESS IS A DOOR NOW, because the step definitions left. Each plugin owns the features it promises and the steps that drive its own surface (`packages/plugins/<name>/e2e/`), and those files are loaded by the same cucumber run as this package's own — so they need the same world, the same waits and the same runner, and they resolve their imports from THEIR package rather than from this one. `./harness/*` is that door: `support/world.ts` is `@olai/tests/harness/world.ts`, and a plugin declares `@olai/tests` in its devDependencies and nothing else. `support/runner.ts` and `support/playwright.ts` are re-exports for exactly that reason — one copy of cucumber registers every step, and playwright's Nix-pinned version stays in ONE manifest. `./agent/*` is the second door: the scripted ACP agents and their session store, which chat's steps drive. What is NOT a door is `features/` or `fixtures/` — a plugin's features are its own, and a fixture corpus is read by path off the served directory, never imported.
//scripts: Bun hosts the runner, and `test` NAMES cucumber's entry file so that it does — never the `cucumber-js` bin, whose `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang is resolved against PATH and hands the suite to whatever node the host has. README.md tells that story; runner.test.ts pins the spelling. Keep it a path: this one is stable because the isolated linker (bunfig.toml) gives every package its own direct dependencies.
//dependencies: WHAT THE HARNESS STANDS ON, which is a shorter list than it was: a row keeps the steps that drive its own surface under its own `e2e/`, so a name only that row's steps need is that row's own file now, reached relatively, with no door and no line here (the mail row's fakes and their fixture tables are NOT that: they are the appliance door `olai-plugin-mail/appliance/testlib`, listed below). Six plugins left this list with their steps (files, identity, layout, and odu's chip ids among them). @olai/web supplies the curated testlib (attributes, deadlines, theme and dates); @olai/bundle supplies the combined testids, which support/testids.ts hands on because a plugin may not import the registry; @olai/fonts and @olai/appearance supply display policy; @olai/ui-primitives supplies shared UI names. @olai/format supplies MARKS and literal test claims, and @olai/surface supplies mediaHref and sealPolicy. support/world.ts composes ROW_TESTID from the testids doors of outlines, markdown, hypertext, csv, image and pdf — one question about six rows at once, which no one of them can answer — and those dependencies are names only, not plugin activations. Chat supplies the panel constants that same file builds a shared selector from, and outlines its record UI contracts. Alerts' and outlines' preference storage keys arrive through support/storage_keys.ts, for the panel that sets them and does not own them. Kolu supplies its fake appliance testlib; odu supplies its fake service testlib; mail its two fakes (a Himalaya binary and a Google origin), which the harness starts for the three `@mail-*` tags and whose fixture NAMES are the plugin's own (`plugins/mail/e2e/steps/mail_fixtures.ts`, read by `support/hooks.ts`). The four ACP engines supply the scripted agents' own protocol constants. @olai/plugin-api supplies the host contracts used by test plugins, and @olai/log supplies the test log collector. These are explicit dependencies of the harness; the bundle's import fences check each allowed static door.
//devDependencies: @olai/log is here for its `./testlib` DECODER only: the readiness signal this suite waits on is a line on the server's stdout, and that line's format belongs to @olai/log — so the thing that reads it back is @olai/log's too, rather than a regex this suite would maintain alone and silently stop matching the day a value needed quoting. playwright is pinned to 1.61.1 — the version of `pkgs.playwright-driver` in the pinned nixpkgs. The npm package ships only the driver's JS; the browsers come from the Nix store via PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, and the driver refuses a browser build it was not compiled against. A minor-version drift here (kolu's 1.59.0, say) does not fail at install time — it fails at `chromium.launch()` with "Executable doesn't exist", pointing at a path inside the store that is real but wrong. Bump this only together with the nixpkgs pin, never on its own.
